home.heroDesc: From a single report, {brand} builds a parallel world of {agentScale} that think, debate and react like real people. Stress-test your campaign, your product or your narrative before launch — and dodge {optimalSolution} with decisions that actually hold up outside the lab.
home.systemReadyDesc: Upload documents, news or reports. Simuloo turns them into a living ecosystem of agents with memory, emotion and judgment of their own.
home.metricHighAvailDesc: Per run, depending on the material you upload
home.step01Desc: We turn your documents into a map of who is who and how they connect.
home.step02Desc: We create people with their own memory, interests and voice.
home.step03Desc: Dozens of people interact in parallel on two social networks, round after round.
home.step04Desc: An analyst reviews everything that happened and writes a report with quotes and arguments.
home.step05Desc: Talk to any simulated person, or to the analyst, to understand the why behind every signal.

padel.title: How will the public react to a padel court-booking app at €4.99/month?
padel.verdict: It appeals, but the price raises doubts: almost everyone would try it free for a month, few would pay before seeing its value.
padel.quote: “If I can book in two taps, I’ll pay. If you make me sign up before I see free courts, I’m gone.”
padel.quoteBy: Interview with a simulated person · casual player
padel.f1: Booking a court without calling anyone: for €4.99 I’m in.
padel.f2: I already spend more on beers after the match. Count me in.
padel.f3: If I can see at once which courts are free, I’ll use it every week.
padel.f4: I’m sending it to the Thursday group right now.
padel.f5: Exactly what I needed to stop chasing people on WhatsApp.
padel.f6: With friends we’d use it every weekend.
padel.u1: I like the idea, but what if my club already has its own app?
padel.u2: Can I try it free for a month before paying?
padel.u3: Depends on how many courts near me show up.
padel.u4: Not sure I’d use it enough to pay every month.
padel.u5: What if the court I want is never free?
padel.u6: I’m in if they tell me what a single booking costs.
padel.a1: Yet another subscription: I already have too many.
padel.a2: I call the club and it’s free.
padel.a3: For one Sunday game a month, it’s not worth it.
padel.a4: I don’t trust leaving my card on a new app.
padel.a5: €4.99 a month for something I already do for free.
padel.a6: I’d rather pay only when I play.

b2b.brief: Invoicing software for small businesses at €29/month
b2b.title: How will small businesses react to invoicing software at €29/month?
b2b.verdict: It wins over those who invoice by hand and saves them hours; those who already have an accountant hesitate to change and want to see the migration before paying.
b2b.quote: “If I can import my spreadsheet invoices in a day, I’ll buy it. If I have to start from scratch, I’ll stay as I am.”
b2b.quoteBy: Interview with a simulated person · small-business manager
b2b.f1: Invoicing in two clicks instead of fighting the spreadsheet: I’ll take it.
b2b.f2: For what an hour of my accountant costs, it pays off.
b2b.f3: If it reminds me of pending payments on its own, it pays for itself.
b2b.f4: We’ll try it at the office this week.
b2b.f5: It takes mandatory e-invoicing off my plate.
b2b.f6: I’m sending it to my partner today.
b2b.u1: Can I bring my old invoices without starting over?
b2b.u2: I like it, but my accountant already uses another program.
b2b.u3: What happens to my data if I stop paying?
b2b.u4: Depends on how many users the price includes.
b2b.u5: Does it connect to my bank?
b2b.u6: I want to see them migrate a real customer before deciding.
b2b.a1: I’ve used my spreadsheet for ten years and it’s never failed me.
b2b.a2: €29 a month for something my accountant already does.
b2b.a3: One more program to learn: I don’t have time.
b2b.a4: I don’t want my company data in a new system.
b2b.a5: I’m afraid of being tied to a subscription.
b2b.a6: There are three of us: not worth it.

precio.brief: 12% price increase at a specialty coffee brand
precio.title: How will customers react to a 12% price increase at a specialty coffee brand?
precio.verdict: Most accept it if the reason is explained and reject it if it arrives unannounced; occasional buyers are the first to leave.
precio.quote: “If they explain it’s for the beans and the growers, I’ll pay. If only the price on the site changes, I’m out.”
precio.quoteBy: Interview with a simulated person · subscription customer
precio.f1: If it’s to pay the growers better, I’ll take it.
precio.f2: Still the best coffee I’ve tried: I’m staying.
precio.f3: One euro more for something I enjoy every morning. Fine.
precio.f4: If there’s an offer for subscribers, I’m staying.
precio.f5: I’d rather this than a drop in quality.
precio.f6: They explained it well, I appreciate that.
precio.u1: Is it only costs, or margin too?
precio.u2: Depends on what the others charge.
precio.u3: If they raise it again in six months, I’m gone.
precio.u4: Do subscribers keep the old price?
precio.u5: I’ll think it over until the next delivery.
precio.u6: They haven’t said what improves with the increase.
precio.a1: 12% with no notice: I’m going to the competition.
precio.a2: My usual coffee at a different price isn’t the same.
precio.a3: I can find a similar one cheaper at the supermarket.
precio.a4: They raise prices and shipping stays the same. Not worth it.
precio.a5: I’m cancelling the subscription this week.
precio.a6: Three increases in two years: that’s it.

crisis.brief: Recall of a yoghurt batch over a quality defect
crisis.title: How will the public react to the recall of a yoghurt batch?
crisis.verdict: It depends on speed and clarity: with an immediate notice and a refund, most keep trusting the brand; if it drags, doubt spreads.
crisis.quote: “I’ll stay if they refund me without paperwork and tell me what went wrong. If they stay silent, I switch brands.”
crisis.quoteBy: Interview with a simulated person · parent
crisis.f1: They warned fast and refund the money: that’s how it’s done.
crisis.f2: I’d rather they recall a batch than stay quiet.
crisis.f3: I’ve bought them for years and they’ve never let me down.
crisis.f4: The statement is clear, I trust it.
crisis.f5: If they refund me without fuss, I’m staying.
crisis.f6: This happens to anyone: what matters is how you respond.
crisis.u1: How many batches are affected, exactly?
crisis.u2: I’ll wait to see what the investigation says.
crisis.u3: With kids at home, I’m not risking it for now.
crisis.u4: Why did they take so long to warn us?
crisis.u5: Depends on how they fix it.
crisis.u6: I’m not sure I trust the statement.
crisis.a1: If one batch slipped through, how many more are undiscovered?
crisis.a2: I’m switching brands: I don’t want to risk it.
crisis.a3: They took far too long to warn us.
crisis.a4: I won’t trust this brand again.
crisis.a5: With kids at home, this is unacceptable.
crisis.a6: I’d rather pay more for a brand that doesn’t fail.

publico.brief: A town council announces a marina on the coast
publico.title: How will residents react to the announcement of a marina on their coast?
publico.verdict: Opinion polarises: jobs and tourism win over some, the impact on the surroundings turns others against it, and many wait to see the environmental study.
publico.quote: “If it brings steady jobs and doesn’t block my beach, I’ll back it. If they don’t show the environmental study, I don’t trust it.”
publico.quoteBy: Interview with a simulated person · local resident
publico.f1: It will bring jobs to an area that needs them.
publico.f2: More tourists means more customers for my bar.
publico.f3: If the marina is done well, it improves the coast.
publico.f5: The environmental study has convinced me.
publico.f6: As long as there are local jobs, count me in.
publico.u1: Where exactly will they build it?
publico.u2: I want to see the whole environmental study.
publico.u3: Who pays: the town or a company?
publico.u4: Depends on how many jobs go to locals.
publico.u5: And the fishing grounds, will they respect them?
publico.u6: I’ll trust it if we all vote on it.
publico.a1: They’ll flatten the trees that have always been here.
publico.a2: We’ll be the ones suffering the noise and traffic.
publico.a3: This isn’t for the town, it’s for a few.
publico.a4: The coast belongs to everyone, it’s not for sale.
publico.a6: I don’t want a marina where my beach used to be.

home.researchHint: Looks up context on your topic —controversies, news, who is involved— and adds it to your document, with sources. Your question and the start of your document are sent to the search engine: don’t turn it on for anything confidential.

home.roundsWhat: A round is one turn of the conversation: normally, one simulated hour. In each one, the people who are active at that hour read what the others have posted and decide whether to write, reply, like or stay quiet. 20 rounds are almost a day of conversation; 72, three days.

home.welcomeBody: A 6-step walkthrough of the home screen so you can launch your first simulation. You can skip it any time and reopen it from the "?" button at the top right.
home.uploadBody: Drop PDFs, Word documents, notes or images describing the world you want to simulate (a brand brief, a plan, meeting notes, etc.). Simuloo extracts entities and relationships to build the graph.
home.nameBody: Optional but recommended: this name appears in the projects list, in the header and in the filename of the report you download at the end.
home.promptTitle: 2. Describe what you want to simulate
home.promptBody: Write the question or scenario in plain language (e.g. "How would millennial moms react to the X launch?"). The engine uses it to plan the report.
home.startBody: Clicking this takes you into the 5-step wizard where you'll watch the graph being built in real time.
home.projectsBody: From here you can jump back into any project you've created, review its graph, simulations and reports.
home.modeBody: Step by step: you review each stage and decide when to continue. Automatic: the server runs all five stages on its own, even if you close the tab.

main1.welcomeBody: You are in Step 1 — graph building. Let me show you the three key zones so you know what's going on.
main1.graphBody: The world Simuloo is building from your initial brief. Nodes = entities, edges = relationships. You can zoom, drag and refresh.
main1.stepBody: Here you drive the current phase: ontology, graph build, system logs. Once Step 1 is done you'll see the button to move on to Step 2.
main1.stepperBody: Shows which step of the flow you're on (1→5). You can go to any step you've already been through, back or ahead; the next ones open as you move forward.
main1.layoutBody: Toggle between: graph-only, split view, or workbench-only. Handy when you want to focus on one of the two zones.

main2.envBody: Here we generate the agent profiles (Twitter + Reddit) that will populate the simulation. Progress appears in the right panel.
main2.nextBody: Once generation finishes, you'll be able to launch the simulation in the next step. The stepper above tells you how far you've come.

sim.welcomeBody: This is where the simulation instance is created and the agent profiles (Twitter + Reddit) are prepared before the real simulation starts.
sim.graphBody: The graph stays visible so you can consult it while configuring the simulation. Use the switcher above to hide it if you need more space.
sim.envBody: Each numbered card represents a phase: instance, profiles, environment initialization. Wait for all of them to turn green before launching.
sim.startBody: Once you've reviewed profiles and set the number of rounds, press "Start dual simulation" to move on to Step 3 (live run).
sim.stepperBody: You're in Step 2 of 5. Go back to review earlier steps; anything that already ran is shown without launching it again.

run.welcomeBody: The agents are now acting in the simulated world. This can take several minutes — here's how to follow along.
run.controlBarBody: Two cards (Info Plaza = Twitter, Topic Community = Reddit) showing current round, simulated time and action count. They turn green when finished.
run.actionsBody: Stop button to interrupt the simulation at any time. When both platforms finish, the "Generate report" button unlocks and takes you to Step 4.
run.timelineBody: Every agent action (POST, LIKE, COMMENT…) appears here in chronological order. Filter by platform or action type to focus on what matters.
run.graphBody: The graph stays available so you can inspect relationships while the simulation is running.

report.welcomeBody: The Report Agent is writing your report section by section, Notion-style. Follow along live to see which step is executing.
report.headerBody: Shows the title, summary and report ID. When everything is done, you can download it as a PDF (named after your project) from Step 5.
report.sectionsBody: Each section is generated in turn. Finished ones are expandable/collapsible; the active one shows a spinner; pending ones are dimmed.
report.workflowBody: Right panel: metrics of the ReACT cycle (how many tool calls, which step is running, agent timeline). Handy for debugging reports that stall.
report.nextBody: Once the report is complete, the stepper takes you to Step 5 — chat with the agents. You'll also find the download buttons there (PDF and text).

interaction.welcomeBody: Here you can chat with the agents, explore the simulated world and send mass surveys. Let me show you the four main tabs.
interaction.reportBody: The full finished report. Use the download buttons (PDF or text) to get a copy named after your project. Click on any section to collapse or expand it.
interaction.actionBarBody: These are the four available tools. The active tab changes what the right-hand panel shows.
interaction.tabReportBody: Talk to the agent that wrote the report. It has access to the graph, InsightForge and the interview summary — use it to ask for deeper analysis.
interaction.tabAgentBody: Pick an agent from the dropdown to talk to them directly. They answer in character (profession, bio, opinions).
interaction.tabExplorerBody: Timeline-style view with each agent's activity during the simulation (posts, likes, comments). Useful to inspect specific behaviors.
interaction.tabSurveyBody: Send a question or survey to all agents at once and receive aggregated responses. Perfect for validating hypotheses with N agents at a time.
interaction.chatInputBody: Press Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a line break. The agent replies in seconds and keeps context throughout the conversation.

brief.missingRequired: Required sections are missing: the simulation will be worse. Complete the document with the template or use the interview.
brief.allRequiredOk: It has the essentials. The more detail about the audience, the better the simulation.
brief.interviewIntro: I'll ask concrete questions, one at a time, until we have what the simulation needs. If an answer is vague I'll push back. You can generate the brief at any time.
brief.composing: Writing the brief with the template…
brief.draftHint: Review and fix anything needed. Anything marked «Pending» couldn't be filled from your answers.
brief.downloadFailed: The document could not be prepared. Please try again.
brief.cardBody: I’ll interview you for a few minutes and write it with the template. A good brief is what improves the simulation most.
